newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign inflows lift Polish zloty to resistance.
newsitem.headline: Foreign inflows lift Polish zloty to resistance.

text.p: The zloty gained steam in late trade as foreign investors purchased Polish fixed bonds and placed bids for T-bills at Monday's auction, dealers said.

They said that foreign inflows buoyed the zloty to key resistance levels around three percent from the trading band centre after importer orders depressed the local unit versus the basekt of currencies in morning trade.

"The zloty first eased under weight of importer orders only to rebound on client orders likely linked with foreign entry into Polish treasuries," said Lukasz Kowalski, dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
The zloty closed at 2.94/2.88 percent from the parity rate, stronger than Friday's 2.87/2.80 percent.
It was at 3.0830/50 to the dollar, up from 3.0840/70 on Friday and at 1.8062/72 to the mark, down from 1.8040/60.

Dealers said that roughly $15 million worth of foreign inflows into T-bills may push the zloty slightly higher on Tuesday but said the threat of a central bank intervention and importers' orders would likely offset any large movements.
On the money market overnight rates eased to close at 21.60/21.80 percent from opening's 21.70/21.90 percent but dealers said the market remained balanced.
Tomorrow/next rates ended flat at 21.65/21.90 percent from this morning's 21.50/21.95 percent.
Dealers expected the minimum price of Poland's 10-year floating rate bond to ease slightly at Tuesday's 600 million zloty primary auction amid small interest from investors.
"Bids should total about a third of the Treasury's offer with minimum and average prices inching down by several basis points on Tuesday," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.
At the last auction of similar 10-year bonds on January 10 the minimum price was 98.51 and the average price was 98.6.
